cases.statement: One Italian family with consanguineous (first-cousin) parents. Homozygous: proband AC and siblings DC and RC, all with almost undetectable HDL. Heterozygous: sister CC and the two sons of DC and AC. Only AC is listed in the batch (TANGIER-ID0037); the other carriers have no batch identity.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Person-level (AC): almost undetectable HDL with very low ApoA1, neuropathy, myocardial infarction, corneal leucomas and foamy histiocytes in colon; the authors argue against LCAT- and APOA1-related HDL deficiency on clinical grounds, but only ABCA1 was sequenced (no other genes reported tested). The authors describe AC's neurological phenotype as peculiar/uncommon. Note that the same paper reports initial signs of dilated cardiomyopathy in AC while using absence of cardiomyopathy to argue against APOA1-related amyloidosis.

quotes.quote: AC, DC, and RC presented almost undetectable HDL cholesterol (HDL-C) and extremely low Apolipoprotein A1 levels in their plasma (Table 2).

However, the presence of neurological symptoms associated with history of tonsillectomy and myocardial infarction, but not of kidney function impairment (which is typical of LCAT-associated FHD) nor cardiomyopathy [which is typical of APOA1-related amyloidosis – (25)] should point toward the diagnosis of ABCA1-associated TD.
Echocardiogram evidenced a reduced global systolic function, with 44% ejection fraction, mild pulmonary hypertension (estimated PAPs 37 mmHg), and initial signs of dilated cardiomyopathy

The clinical phenotype of AC was peculiar being characterized by a syringomyelic-like anesthesia with electrophysiological findings of a demyelinating neuropathy with secondary axonal loss and small fibers involvement.

segregation.statement: Three affected siblings (AC, DC, RC) are homozygous and have almost undetectable HDL and ApoA1. One sister (CC) is heterozygous with HDL 44 mg/dl and low ApoA1, and has some cardiac and sensory complaints. Two sons of DC and AC are heterozygous (phenotype not reported). Parents (first cousins) not reported tested; two brothers died in infancy (not tested).

functional.statement: No functional assay of this variant; the authors state they did not evaluate its functional effect. Only an in-silico prediction of the truncated protein is given (see computational_predictions).

quotes.quote: Unfortunately, we did not directly evaluate the functional effect of this mutation.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense (stop-gain) variant, p.(Tyr1698Ter), per the batch HGVS; the paper places it in exon 37 and expects a truncated protein lacking the last four intramembrane repeats. The paper describes TD as caused by loss-of-function ABCA1 mutations. It does not discuss nonsense-mediated decay.

quotes.quote: It was a novel mutation introducing a stop codon in the exon 37 of ABCA1 gene.
It was expected to generate a truncated protein, missing the last four intramembrane repeats (Figure 2C).
Truncated protein might not be expressed on cytoplasmic membrane and be discarded in the endoplasmic reticulum.
Tangier disease is inherited as an autosomal recessive disorder, and affected patients are expected to have LOF mutations in both alleles of ABCA1 gene.

computational_predictions.statement: Only an in-silico translation of the truncated protein (ExPASy Translate) is reported for this variant; no SIFT/PolyPhen or splice scores are given for it.

quotes.quote: In particular, the in silico prediction of truncated protein was obtained by the ExPASY Translate tool.

authors_classification.statement: No ACMG classification; the authors present it as a novel mutation causing Tangier disease.

quotes.quote: A Novel Mutation in ABCA1 Gene Causing Tangier Disease in an Italian Family with Uncommon Neurological Presentation
The reported ABCA1 mutation has never been described before in a Tangier family.

concerns: Paper uses transcript NM_005502.3 (and NP_005493.2); batch HGVS is on NM_005502.4. Legacy name Y1698X also used.
Five further carriers in the same paper (DC and RC homozygous; CC and the two sons heterozygous) have no identity in the batch; they appear in the extraction but were not attached to this candidate.
The paper says 'the two sons of DC and AC' without saying which son belongs to whom.
In the proband, 'several polymorphisms and functionally uncharacterized sequence variations' were also found and dismissed by the authors after in-silico analysis; they are not listed.

Paper contradicts itself on cardiomyopathy: AC's echocardiogram shows 'initial signs of dilated cardiomyopathy', yet absence of cardiomyopathy is used to argue against APOA1-related amyloidosis. Only ABCA1 was sequenced.
Heterozygous sister CC has cardiac valve replacement, paresthesia and focal weakness/hypoesthesia; the authors do not discuss whether these relate to carrier status.
notes_for_panel: Consanguineous Italian family: three homozygous siblings with almost undetectable HDL/ApoA1 and neuropathy/cardiac disease; one heterozygous sister with low ApoA1 and two heterozygous sons. No functional, population or formal ACMG data; transcript NM_005502.3 in the paper.
